issues.note: False closed set. The front asserts the exam rules out exactly TWO explanations; Domain-1_v2 §1.6 rules out THREE: 'Not: web-search agent query quality, synthesis agent gap detection, document analysis filters.' The back names only query quality and document filters and silently drops synthesis-agent gap detection. A learner who correctly recalls all three would mark himself wrong, and a learner who drills this card learns that synthesis gap detection is a live candidate root cause when the corpus explicitly excludes it.

d1-037 already asks this exact question with the correct count: 'Which three components are NOT the root cause? The web-search agent's query quality, the synthesis agent's gap detection, and the document-analysis filters.' d1-110 is a strictly worse twin of d1-037, and the two cards contradict each other on the same list (two vs three). d1-036, d1-040 and d1-100 also cover the §1.6 / Key-Distinctions #7 root-cause rule.

Primary cite is Key-Distinctions_v1 #7, which states the root-cause rule (decomposition, not subagent capability) but enumerates no ruled-out explanations at all. The list the back is drawn from lives only in Domain-1_v2 §1.6, which is cited second. If the card were kept, the order must be Domain-1_v2 §1.6 first.

d2-053 already drills this exact fact: 'After an Edit fails on a non-unique anchor, a teammate retries with a shorter, more generic anchor string. What happens? The odds get worse: a shorter string is likelier to occur in several places, so the same failure repeats.' d2-073 is that card reworded as a 'why' question.

The card is a compound of three existing cards rather than one retrievable fact. Sentence one duplicates d2-053; sentence two ('Read plus Write is the sanctioned fallback') is the entire answer to d2-052; the trap's second clause ('`sed` through Bash bypasses the tool built for the job') is the entire answer to d2-054. Nothing in it is new to the deck.

Byte-identical duplicate of d3-060. Same front, same back, same single cite (Domain-3_v2 §3.12), same tags, same core/rev flags. Not a near-duplicate - the same card twice in one deck file. This is also evidence the late batch got no dedup pass at all.

Secondary, and it applies to d3-060 as well: type is `fact`, but CARD-SPEC §4 defines `fact` as 'a number, a flag, a filename, an exact value. Short front, short back.' This is a two-part mechanism contrast with a 170-character back, i.e. a `concept`. The content itself is accurate against Domain-3_v2 §3.12: `--resume` resumes a previous named session with saved context, and `fork_session` creates a branch where both forks inherit context to the branch point then diverge. No factual defect.

Collides with d3-003, which carries the same corpus scenario and the same answer: 'Three developers get a coding convention applied automatically and a fourth does not... In the original developers' `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md`... Moving it to the project-level config fixes it.' d3-004 and d3-064 also state the version-controlled-vs-one-machine rule from Key-Distinctions #1.

The front already places the convention in `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md`, which is the half of the exam item that has to be diagnosed. What remains ('move it to project level') is handed over by the setup. CARD-SPEC §10 forbids putting the answer in the front.

The trap invents a distractor. 'A per-user config cache' is not a documented Claude Code mechanism and appears nowhere in Domain-3_v2 §3.1 or Key-Distinctions #1, whose recorded wrong answers are about location and version control, not caching or stale checkouts. CARD-SPEC §10: do not invent flags, parameters, or behaviors.

Collides with d3-008, whose back already contains this card's entire payload: 'Run `/memory` to see which memory files are loaded in each session; the file holding that convention is usually missing from one of them.' d3-080 differs only in naming `/memory` in the front instead of the back. Content is otherwise accurate and supported by Domain-3_v2 §3.1. Re-angle it onto the documented anti-pattern, which no other card fronts, or drop it and keep d3-008.

suggested.text: Claude keeps skipping a convention, so a developer restates it more forcefully in every prompt. What does that leave unchecked?

issues.note: Matching back for the re-angle above, so the card stops restating d3-008.

suggested.text: Whether the file holding that convention is in the session's loaded memory set at all. `/memory` lists what is loaded.

issues.note: Same ask-shape and same answer as d3-018: 'A codebase-analysis skill produces so much output that Claude loses track of the original task. Which frontmatter change fixes it? `context: fork`, which runs the skill in an isolated subagent context so its output stays out of the main conversation.' d3-081 swaps in the other §3.3 exam scenario as dressing but tests the identical retrieval. d3-015, d3-019, d3-021 and d3-069 already give the deck five `context: fork` cards. The back's claims are accurate against Domain-3_v2 §3.3; the defect is redundancy, not fact.

If kept, the cite order is inverted. The specifics the card carries - the isolated subagent context, the summary returned to the main conversation, and both trap distractors (splitting the skill, switching to a faster model) - all come from Domain-3_v2 §3.3. Key-Distinctions #13 is a scope table that mentions none of them and should be the second cite.

The primary cite contradicts the card. Key-Distinctions_v1 #14's table row reads 'Multi-turn tool calls: Not supported - fire-and-forget', which is precisely the blanket claim this card's trap declares false. The claim the back actually makes lives in Domain-4_v2 §4.11 'Accuracy Note: Tool Use in Batches' ('the Batch API does support tool use and multi-turn conversations... what batches cannot do is interactive back-and-forth within one request's processing'), and is confirmed by CURRENT-DOCS-DELTA_v1.md §D5. Cite §4.11 alone; keeping #14 points the learner at the outdated framing.

The front restates d4-054: 'A batch request defines tools and the response comes back with a `tool_use` block. Why can your client not answer it and continue inside that same batch item?' Re-angle the front onto the supported-vs-unsupported split, which no existing d4 card asks, so the card earns the trap field d4-054 lacks.

suggested.text: Which part of tool use does a Batches API request support, and which part does it not?

issues.note: Matching back for the re-angled front. The precise limitation is preserved and the flattened 'batches do not support tools' reading stays excluded.

suggested.text: It supports `tools` definitions and multi-turn histories; it cannot pause mid-request for the client to run the tool and return a `tool_result`.

issues.note: d5-031 already contains this card's entire back inside its own: 'An extraction system reports 97% overall accuracy and the team wants to auto-process everything above the confidence threshold. What has to be checked first? Accuracy broken out by document type and by field - an aggregate figure can hide a rare document type failing 40% of the time.' Same 97/40 pair, same §5.9 source, and d5-031 additionally supplies the action. The trap's two rejected audit strategies are covered by d5-032's stratified-sampling back. The card is factually correct against Domain-5_v2 §5.9; it just adds nothing the deck lacks.
